div.head: Ps Cn for 3.1
div.ab: Mediocresque tales post ferarum curam susceptam pro liberalibus semper habeantur, quos Dani ealdermen appellant.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 621 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)
div.ab: And let such middling men, after they have taken on the care of the beasts, always be held as nobles, whom the Danes call ealdermen.

note.seg: Überfreie, Adlige (mehr als liber in 5) auch sonst im 12. Jh.; vgl. S. 613i. Dieses Aufsteigen des Standes durch Forstdienst erfand Verf. vielleicht aus Reminiscenzen an Angelsächs. Wergelderhöhung durch Königsdienst. Thatsächlich gewährte höherer Forstdienst wohl verstärkten Schutz, hob aber zum Adel höchstens gesellschaftlich, nicht rechtlich

More than free, noble (more than liber in 5), elsewhere too in the 12th century; cf. p. 613 n. i. The author perhaps invented this rise in rank through forest service from recollections of the Anglo-Saxon raising of wergeld through the king's service. In fact higher forest service probably gave increased protection, but raised a man to the nobility at most socially, not legally.

ebenso u. 21; ealdorman heisst bei den Angelsachsen Fürst, Herzog, Graf, was Verf. nicht meint, seit 12. Jh. auch Amtsperson beschränkterer Geltung, Vornehmer, wohl aber nie, was hier behauptet, Vollfreien-Stand

Likewise below, 21; among the Anglo-Saxons ealdorman means prince, duke, earl, which the author does not mean; from the 12th century also an official of more limited standing, a man of rank, but probably never, as asserted here, the rank of the fully free.
